storyboard.claim: Teller's blood bond to his mother is unchosen and he grieves it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller slumped beside Luther, two bonded men.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the parallel between Teller and Luther.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pairs two men bound against their will.
storyboard.staging: Teller slumps in grief beside Luther.

storyboard.claim: Luther's magic bond to Diem is unchosen, dragging him into wars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon beside Luther thinking over his bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read as a bond imposed, not chosen.
storyboard.staging: Luther broods, worried, beside the chains icon.

storyboard.claim: The men's autonomy is taken because of the women they are bonded to.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teller thinking, worried, in a stage setting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why both men are dragged into the wars.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the cause of the lost autonomy.
storyboard.staging: Teller broods over the bond that controls him.

storyboard.claim: The throne room scene is one of the most visceral set pieces.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lumnos seen across a wide sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition to the throne room scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the set piece as the next scene.
storyboard.staging: Lumnos on the horizon introduces the scene.

storyboard.claim: The throne room air is thick with burning cedar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fire icon in the throne room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the scene the narrator describes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fire icon makes the burning literal.
storyboard.staging: Fire icon over the throne room stage.

storyboard.claim: Smoke curls around the furious Ignos Regent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Smoke and flames rising over the empty throne room.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smoke is the visible cost of the scene.
storyboard.staging: Smoke fills the empty stage.

storyboard.claim: Diem sets nine ancient wooden thrones on fire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Nine thrones burning in the throne room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The act itself after the setup.
storyboard.addedInformation: Nine thrones makes the scale concrete.
storyboard.staging: Burning thrones fill the stage.

storyboard.claim: The aristocrats stumble backward, stunned, lit by the orange glow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the crowd's shock.
storyboard.staging: Recoiling figures lit orange by the fire.

storyboard.claim: The thrones are political symbols, not just chairs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Burning thrones on the stage as symbols.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the symbolism the thrones carry.
storyboard.staging: Thrones on the stage stand for power.

storyboard.claim: The thrones represent 900 years of systemic oppression.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the duration of the oppression.
storyboard.staging: Thrones carry the weight of centuries.

callout.text: BURN DOWN THE SEAT OF POWER

storyboard.claim: Leadership sometimes has to burn down the seat of power.
storyboard.onScreenText: BURN DOWN THE SEAT OF POWER
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why Diem burns the thrones.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fire is the literal means of destruction.
storyboard.staging: Fire icon over the empty seat of power.

storyboard.claim: The architecture of oppression must be eradicated.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage setting of the old order.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the system to tear down.
storyboard.staging: The old stage stands for the system.

storyboard.claim: Taran and Eleanor recruit younger descended from the 20 houses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Taran pointing with an angry, severe face.
storyboard.addedInformation: Taran is the recruiter named in the narration.
storyboard.staging: Taran points, angry, at the recruits.

storyboard.claim: Progyny laws are draconian breeding regulations for the 20 houses.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines the law's purpose.
storyboard.staging: Stage holds the law's name.

storyboard.claim: Only the primary heir is safe; the diluted are treated as expendable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter buckets: primary heir, diluted bloodline, expendable.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows how the law sorts people.
storyboard.staging: Sorter buckets split the people by bloodline.

storyboard.claim: The younger faction calls itself the embers because its politics is arson.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Taran pointing, angry, as the faction's leader.
storyboard.addedInformation: The name is the narrator's own wordplay on arson.
storyboard.staging: Taran points, angry, at the name of the faction.

storyboard.claim: The faction wants to burn the progyny laws from inside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage with the law's name as the target.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the goal explicit.
storyboard.staging: The stage holds the target of the burning.

storyboard.claim: Diem takes power back by destroying a corrupt system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the destruction as the narrator's catharsis.
storyboard.staging: Stage shows the corrupt system.

storyboard.claim: As war logistics, the throne burning is an absolute disaster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lumnos seen across a wide sky.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the same act as a logistical failure.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over Lumnos.

storyboard.claim: Diem faces a war against Ofyuk, an ancient god amassing an army.
storyboard.addedInformation: War icon shows the conflict literally.
storyboard.staging: War icon on the horizon.

storyboard.claim: A war needs supply lines, steel, rations and funded battalions.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the logistics a war requires.
storyboard.staging: Empty stage; callout carries the list.

storyboard.claim: Burning the thrones alienates the aristocracy who fund the war.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stage with the burned throne room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the cost of the burning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the act that alienates the aristocracy.
storyboard.staging: Stage of the humiliation.

storyboard.claim: The aristocracy is the group Diem needs to fund the campaign.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identifies the funders.
storyboard.staging: Stage holds the aristocracy in view.

storyboard.claim: Tactically, burning the thrones is a terrible move.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the narrator's tactical verdict.
storyboard.staging: Burned stage carries the verdict.

storyboard.claim: Burning thrones causes alienated aristocrats and burned supply chains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow from burning thrones to lost supply.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause-effect chain.
storyboard.staging: Flow arrows show the chain.

storyboard.claim: Diem's bond with Luther demands a new world.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks why Diem burns the system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the bond to the politics.
storyboard.staging: Luther thinks over the bond.

storyboard.claim: Luther is a half-mortal outcast the elite system rejects.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the system rejects Diem's bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names Luther's status.
storyboard.staging: Luther slumps, sad, outcast.

callout.text: THE BOND KEEPS DIEM FROM RULING

storyboard.claim: Diem cannot rule the system while bonded to Luther.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE BOND KEEPS DIEM FROM RULING
storyboard.addedInformation: States the consequence of the bond.
storyboard.staging: Luther stands sad beside the callout.

storyboard.claim: Rejecting the old system bankrupts Diem's war effort.
storyboard.addedInformation: War icon shows the effort at stake.
storyboard.staging: War icon on the stage.

storyboard.claim: The consequence is an immediate public reckoning Diem faces.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the reckoning.
storyboard.staging: Stage for the reckoning.

storyboard.claim: Diem walks the streets and meets Martha Hanover and the citizens of Lumnos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Lumnos seen across a wide sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the throne room to the streets.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the meeting in the streets of Lumnos.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over the streets.

storyboard.claim: The citizens are covered in soot, not awe.
storyboard.addedInformation: Soot is the visible sign of the fire.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over the sooty city.

storyboard.claim: The citizens demand where their queen was when their homes burned.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the question in the citizens' words.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky, the question in the callout.

storyboard.claim: Grand destiny matters nothing to a person sweeping up the ashes of their home.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the ashes the concrete cost.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over the ashes.

storyboard.claim: Leadership at its core is local.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the principle directly.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky, the principle in the callout.

storyboard.claim: Leadership is a physical contract: a leader must be present when fire falls.
storyboard.addedInformation: Defines leadership as presence.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over the contract.

storyboard.claim: Fancy titles are worthless when the leader is absent.
storyboard.addedInformation: Trophy shows the titles at stake.
storyboard.staging: Trophy on the stage.

storyboard.claim: Half of Fortos is reduced to rubble while Diem is absent.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the scale of the destruction.
storyboard.staging: Wide sky over Fortos.

storyboard.claim: The vice generals bicker over authority.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the generals' conflict.
storyboard.staging: Stage for the bickering.

storyboard.claim: Battalions are sent out with conflicting orders to face Ofyuk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the conflicting orders.
storyboard.staging: Horizon for the battalions' march.
